info.name: Student Management System API
info.description:
Complete API collection for the Student Management System (Spring Boot + JWT).

**How to use**
1. Start MySQL + backend (`mvn spring-boot:run`) on http://localhost:8080
2. Import this collection (and the environment file).
3. Run the whole collection with the Collection Runner (top to bottom). Folder 1 logs in and stores all tokens; every other request picks the right token automatically.
4. Each request has tests that assert the expected status code (incl. 400/401/403/404/409 cases).

Demo accounts: admin@sms.com / Admin@123, lecturer@sms.com / Lecturer@123, student@sms.com / Student@123

item.name: 1. Auth
item.description: Registration, login and current-user. Run these first: they save all tokens used by the other folders.

request.description: Public. Role is optional (defaults to STUDENT). Saves newStudentToken / newStudentId.

exec: pm.test("Message contains \"Admin accounts cannot be created\"", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.include("Admin accounts cannot be created"); });

request.description: Admin accounts cannot be created via registration.

exec: pm.test("Message contains \"Invalid email or password\"", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.include("Invalid email or password"); });

item.name: 2. Users (ADMIN only)
item.description: User management. Every endpoint here needs an ADMIN token.

exec: pm.test("All are LECTURER", function () { pm.response.json().forEach(u => pm.expect(u.role).to.eql("LECTURER")); });

request.description: Password required on create. Saves createdUserId.

request.description: Each course has enrolledCount and 'enrolled' (true if this student is enrolled).
Lecturer is auto-assigned as course owner. Saves lecturerCourseId.
